newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian civil court does not want war crimes trial.
newsitem.headline: Italian civil court does not want war crimes trial.

text.p: An Italian war crimes case against former SS captain Erich Priebke was left without a court to be heard in on Sunday after a civilian prosecutor said he had no jurisdiction.

Italo Ormanni, deputy Rome public prosecutor, referred the controversial case back to a preliminary examining judge with a recommendation that Italy's highest court, the Court of Cassation, be asked to decide whether Priebke should be tried in civilian or military court.

Ormanni was assigned the case on December 5 when a panel of military judges concluded that a civil court should decide whether Priebke was guilty of complicity in murder in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity.
Their ruling brought Priebke's case into line with that of another SS veteran, former major Karl Hass, whose trial is being sought in Italy for the same atrocity.

Priebke and Hass are both accused of complicity in multiple murder for their acknowledged participation in the Ardeatine Caves massacre south of Rome in March 1944, when 335 men and boys were shot in reprisal for a partisan bomb attack.

Priebke, 83, has faced a military court in Rome, but the trial, dogged by legal challenges, ended in uproar in August when the court found Priebke guilty but ruled he was no longer liable for punishment. The verdict was later overturned and a new trial ordered.
Ormanni said he believed a military rather than a civilian court should handle the case because the SS was made up of soldiers and therefore was part of the armed forces.
Priebke and Hass argue that they were under orders to take part in the massacre and would have been killed had they refused.
